SddReviewLifecycle.Mission: Establish approval #1 for the complete actual spec set. One fresh independent reviewer judges semantic coherence; the operator approves the reviewed artifacts. Resume uses only durable artifacts.
SddReviewLifecycle.BeliefState:
Inherited from the loading directive (already in context): ARTIFACT_APPROVAL_FLOW, ARTIFACT_APPROVAL_MARKER, AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_STATELESS_FLOW, AX_TOOL_INVOCATION
Every fix must be operator-approved before execution. The plan is shown as a table. No edits are made before explicit operator "yes" / "go" / "ok". Operator may edit the plan (remove items, change classification, add notes).
Five critic results is the hard automatic cap. At the fifth result — regardless of sensor verdict — the operator must dispose the cycle before readiness or another dispatch. If that round made no edits, the choices are `CLEAN`, `CONTINUE THROUGH ROUND N` with an explicit higher cap, or `RESTART: reason`; if it made edits, CLEAN is unavailable because the changed bytes have not been reviewed, so only CONTINUE or RESTART are offered. A raised cap behaves identically when reached. The sensor cannot authorize continuation, and continuation is never readiness. Uncertainty alone is NOT a blocking finding. ACCEPT only an artifact gap backed by concrete evidence — a cited requirement, invariant, or scenario, naming what concretely breaks, for whom, and when. A preference, alternative design, missing local convention, or question without concrete breakage → REJECT as blocking; when it originates in confusion, classify it through `AX_CONFUSION_BUG` first.

Step.Goal: Identify the complete spec set whose meaning is being approved.
Step.Action: Use actual spec paths and their current content. Set approval #1 to `pending` in every member of the reviewed set. Include every changed parent, child, interface, infrastructure, or dependent spec needed to judge consistency. Do not review a prose plan or a subset that hides cross-spec effects. Per `AX_STATELESS_FLOW`, this durable set is the whole review state. Run the owning structural/integrity checks first.

Step.Goal: Obtain one semantic judgment independent from the author.
Step.Action:
Load `critic-protocol.directive.xml`, then dispatch one fresh reviewer with its full contents as the reviewer's own governing instructions, plus the exact bounded spec set and `Polish: ` (on only when the operator explicitly asked for polish/nits this round; off by default). The reviewer reads but never edits. It checks requirements, negative/failure behavior, interfaces, dependencies, invariants, verification strategy, contradictions, and missing decisions. It returns `CLEAN` or at most five evidence-backed findings naming file and anchor. The reviewer reads only the exact target specs plus the operator brief supplied in its prompt; it does not read flow directives, examples, repository history, source code, or search the repository. It performs one semantic pass and returns the verdict without restating the route or narrating its internal analysis.
The author may mentally inspect its own work before this dispatch, but that does not count as independent review. Do not serialize a plan into JSON, retain the reviewer, or track anything about prior rounds beyond the bare `AX_CAP_5` count STEP_3_RECONCILE keeps.

Step.Goal: Make the proposed specs match accepted review conclusions.
Step.Action:
Per `AX_DEFAULT_ACCEPT`, classify each returned finding before acting on it: ACCEPT only an artifact gap backed by concrete evidence naming what breaks, for whom, and when; REJECT a preference, alternative design, missing local convention, or unevidenced question — uncertainty alone never blocks. For each ACCEPTed finding, correct the owning spec; for each REJECTed one, present a concrete disagreement to the operator instead of editing. Run structural checks after edits. Any semantic edit resets the applicable approval markers to `pending` and therefore requires one fresh STEP_2 review of the new complete target. Give that reviewer the prior findings and corrected target; it verifies those fixes plus one contradiction sweep, then returns `CLEAN` or at most five remaining findings. This is a new bounded verification, not continuation of a reviewer session and not a reason to reload unrelated artifacts.
Per `AX_CAP_5`, this STEP_2⇄STEP_3 review⇄reconcile cycle is bounded, not open-ended: count every STEP_2 dispatch across the whole review. At the fifth result — regardless of that result's verdict — stop dispatching and put an explicit disposition to the operator before another STEP_2 call or STEP_4 approval: `CLEAN` only when that fifth round made no edits; otherwise `CONTINUE THROUGH ROUND N` naming an explicit higher cap, or `RESTART: reason`. A raised cap is bounded the same way when it is in turn reached. The reviewer's verdict never authorizes continuation past the cap by itself.

Step.Goal: Ask the operator to approve the reviewed specifications.
Step.Action: Present a compact decision card: exact spec paths, key requirements and negative scenarios, dependencies/interfaces, verification promises, independent verdict, and accepted risks. Ask `Approve specs` or `Return for correction` per `AX_OPERATOR_AGREEMENT`. On approval, update the human-readable approval #1 Decision Log markers exactly as `ARTIFACT_APPROVAL_MARKER` defines. Record durable product/architecture decisions in the same specs; do not record workflow state outside those artifacts. A new session checks marker shape mechanically and uses Git evidence plus semantic judgment to detect staleness; it never computes a fingerprint.
